sections.title: The Plot Against Jesus
observations: The chief priests and elders conspire to arrest Jesus secretly, fearing a public uproar.
This section highlights the growing tension between Jesus and the religious leaders, who feel threatened by His popularity and teachings.

sections.title: The Anointing at Bethany
observations: A woman anoints Jesus with costly perfume, illustrating true devotion.

Criticism from the disciples shows a contrast between worldly values and the profound significance of worship. Jesus defends her actions, indicating that the gospel will always remember this act of honor.

sections.title: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus
observations: Judas Iscariot’s betrayal is driven by greed, a chilling reminder of the darkness that can dwell in the hearts of even the closest followers of Christ.
This event demonstrates the fulfillment of prophecy and God’s sovereignty in the unfolding plan of salvation.

sections.title: The Last Supper
observations: During the Passover meal, Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, establishing a new covenant in His blood.
This moment encapsulates the core of Christian faith, signifying Jesus’ sacrificial death and the establishment of a new relationship between God and humanity.

sections.title: Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial
observations: Here, Jesus foretells Peter’s denial, illustrating human fragility even in the face of devotion.
Peter’s bold claim of loyalty contrasts sharply with his eventual weakness, serving as a caution against self-reliance.

sections.title: Gethsemane: Jesus' Agony in Prayer
observations: Jesus reveals His human nature by expressing deep anguish over His impending crucifixion. His prayer exemplifies submission to the Father’s will despite personal sorrow.
The disciples’ inability to stay awake reflects spiritual lethargy, emphasizing the need for vigilance in prayer.

sections.title: The Arrest of Jesus
observations: Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss, a poignant act of treachery.
The arrest showcases the fulfillment of prophecy and sets in motion the events leading to the crucifixion. Jesus’ calm demeanor contrasts sharply with the violent actions of the soldiers.

sections.title: Jesus Before Caiaphas
observations: In a mock trial, Jesus faces false accusations and public ridicule, revealing the unjust treatment of those who challenge the religious status quo.
Peter’s denials reinforce the theme of fear and confusion among Jesus’ followers, demonstrating the struggle between faith and fear.

importantVerses.commentary: This verse highlights the significance of the new covenant and the atoning work of Christ.
Jesus’ explanation of His arrest underscores the fulfillment of Scripture and His authority over the situation.

questions: What does the act of the woman anointing Jesus reveal about true worship?
How does the narrative of Judas' betrayal serve as a warning for Christians today?
In what ways does the Last Supper redefine the understanding of covenant in the Old and New Testaments?
What can we learn from Peter’s denial in relation to our own faith and weaknesses?
How does Jesus’ time in Gethsemane encourage us in our moments of distress?
